user.title: VTherm Smart Boiler
user.description: Monitors your boiler; it writes nothing to the boiler until you enable control in the options. Pick a name and the level of detail.

data_description.name: Shown as the device name.
data_description.level: Simple shows the essentials with cautious defaults; advanced shows every parameter. The level changes only what you see, never how the plugin behaves.

signals.title: Boiler signals
signals.description: Pick the entity that provides each signal. None is required: flame and flow temperature enable the burner's metrics, the boiler link and control of the water temperature, which needs both; every other signal enables more of the monitor. A home with only a relay is monitored too. The plugin only reads these entities. One entity feeds one signal only.

data.boiler_lockout: Boiler lockout (a fault that stops the boiler)

data_description.flame: On while the burner burns. Every burner-cycle metric comes from it: the wrong entity gives wrong starts and burn times.
data_description.flow: Water leaving the boiler. Used for hot water availability, emitter power and telling DHW runs from heating; with control, it is part of the boiler link. The wrong entity misleads all of them.
data_description.return: Water coming back to the boiler. Enables the condensing share; without it condensing cannot be judged. The wrong entity gives a wrong condensing share.
data_description.modulation: Burner modulation in percent. With the boiler's power range it estimates heat output and gas use. A sensor in another unit is refused.
data_description.dhw_active: On while the boiler heats domestic hot water. Without it DHW runs are inferred with less certainty and some may count as heating; with control, hot-water charging is then less sure to pause learning.
data_description.pressure: Enables the high-pressure and "add water" notifications and the falling-pressure warning. From an OpenTherm Gateway a reading of 0 bar counts as unknown (the gateway shows 0 after a restart); from any other sensor it is a reading. The wrong entity gives false alarms or none.
data_description.outdoor: The boiler's own outdoor sensor. Used for degree-days, for control's curve, and checked against the weather entity: one found stuck or far off is left out of the curve. A wrong sensor bends the curve until the check catches it.
data_description.ch_setpoint: The flow setpoint the boiler works to, a temperature. Helps tell DHW runs from heating.
data_description.ch_active: On while the boiler heats the rooms. Helps tell DHW from heating when there is no DHW signal.
data_description.pump_running: On while the heating pump runs. Enables the low-flow warning: every valve closed while the pump runs.
data_description.flue_gas: Enables the flue gas alarm and the early warning of a fouling heat exchanger.
data_description.gas_meter: A cumulative gas or energy meter. Gives measured gas per degree-day instead of an estimate. Gas the meter counts while the burner is off (a cooker, another appliance) is shown apart; gas they use while the burner runs cannot be told apart and counts as heating.
data_description.room_setpoint: The room setpoint of a wall thermostat on the gateway, from the thermostat's side — e.g. "Room setpoint 1" on the gateway's thermostat device, or the firmware's TrSet_thermostat with separate sources on; not the gateway's climate target. Shown as the temperature the wall thermostat keeps after a hand-back.
data_description.room_temperature: The room temperature a wired thermostat sends to the boiler, if there is one. Recorded for the assessment.
data_description.weather: Its forecasts are recorded for later forecast features, and its temperature stands in for a missing or suspect outdoor sensor — for degree-days and control's curve. No data leaves your Home Assistant.
data_description.boiler_power: Optional: the boiler's electric power, e.g. from a plug that measures it; used only as proof that a relay-driven boiler heats.
data_description.low_pressure_fault: Optional: the boiler's own low-water-pressure fault, e.g. the gateway's "Low water pressure" on its boiler device. While it reads on for 5 minutes, control switches heating off — without handing the boiler back — and on again when it clears, as the boiler itself does. Unknown or unavailable counts as no fault. Pick only the boiler's own report: a wrong pick stops heating while the boiler could heat. On an OpenTherm Gateway it counts only while the boiler's fault indication (below) is on: the gateway reads the fault details only when a fault appears, and shows them unknown after a restart until the next fault.
data_description.boiler_lockout: Optional: a fault your boiler's manual says stops the boiler (a lockout); not a general fault or service indication, which would stop heating needlessly — on some boilers even the fault indication is only a warning. While it reads on for 5 minutes, control switches heating off — without handing the boiler back — and on again when it clears, as the boiler itself does. Unknown or unavailable counts as no fault. Pick only the boiler's own report: a wrong pick stops heating while the boiler could heat. EMS-ESP has no such signal: it needs a template binary sensor built from your boiler's service codes. On an OpenTherm Gateway a fault detail such as "Gas fault" counts only while the boiler's fault indication (below) is on; its "Fault indication" itself, picked here, counts alone.
data_description.fault_indication: Optional: the boiler's general fault indication, e.g. the gateway's "Fault indication" on its boiler device. It stops nothing by itself. On an OpenTherm Gateway the two fault signals above count only while it reads on — the gateway reads their details once per new fault and never after it clears, so alone they could keep heating off after the boiler has recovered; without it they are not used there. Elsewhere it is not needed.

boiler.title: Boiler
boiler.description: What you know about your boiler. Leave unknown values empty: the plugin then says what it cannot judge.

data.class: What the boiler's integration can do

data_description.class: Flow setpoint, curve parameters only, on/off or read-only. Control (experimental): a flow setpoint (water temperature) or on/off (relay); the other classes are monitored only.
data_description.dhw: None, a storage tank or a combi boiler; required. Used to interpret burns: with "none" every burn counts as heating — declared on a boiler that heats hot water, its draws would count as heating starts; the wrong type counts hot water as heating or the reverse.
data_description.condensing: Condensing boilers get flue gas limits for condensing appliances and are judged on how often they condense; for other boilers the absolute flue gas alarm is off and condensing plays no part in the verdict. The wrong choice warns too late or for nothing, and misjudges the verdict.
data_description.boiler_min_power: Lowest heating power from the manual, in kW. Compared with the building load: a load often below it means the boiler must cycle. A wrong value skews that judgement in the verdict.
data_description.boiler_max_power: Highest heating power in kW. With the minimum and the modulation it estimates heat output; a wrong value skews heat and gas estimates.
data_description.max_ch_setpoint: Highest flow temperature in heating, in °C. Flow above it points to a DHW run; set too low, heating counts as hot water. Control never writes a setpoint above it either: set too low, rooms stay cold in hard frost.
data_description.gas_at_min_power: Gas per hour at minimum power, in your gas meter's unit. With the modulation it estimates gas use when there is no meter; a wrong value skews gas per degree-day.
data_description.gas_at_max_power: Gas per hour at maximum power, in the same unit; a wrong value skews the gas estimates.
data_description.modulation_scale: Whether 0 % is the minimum power (the OpenTherm definition) or the value is a percentage of maximum power. The wrong choice skews heat and gas estimates.
data_description.bypass: Tick when the heating water always has a path — an automatic bypass valve or a low-loss header: the low-flow warning is then off, as closed valves cannot stop the flow. Left unticked on such a system, the warning is false; ticked without one, a real dead-end goes unwarned.

circuit.title: Heating circuit {number}
circuit.description: How this circuit's water temperature is set.

data_description.control: Unmixed, straight from the boiler; mixed through the boiler (a second circuit the boiler mixes); mixed by a separate controller; or a thermostatic mixing valve (fixed). Control runs only for one circuit fed straight from the boiler, or through a fixed valve. The wrong type makes control refuse, or misjudge what reaches the rooms.
data_description.max_flow: The most this circuit may receive, in °C, e.g. underfloor heating on an unmixed loop: control never asks for more, but the boiler may overshoot it by its own hysteresis — set the alarm below to be told. Needed for underfloor on an unmixed loop. Too high overheats the floor.
data_description.fixed_temperature: Needed for a thermostatic mixing valve (fixed): its setting in °C. The boiler's water is kept at least 5 K above it, so the mixing valve can reach it; set higher than the valve's setting, the water runs hotter than needed.
data_description.max_flow_alarm: Information alarm when the measured flow stays above this, in °C. Starts at the maximum + 5 °C. Needs a flow reading. Too high lets a real overshoot pass unreported.
data_description.max_flow_alarm_min: How long, in minutes, before the alarm rises. Starts at 10. Too short reports every overshoot of the boiler's hysteresis.
data_description.flow_entity: A mixed circuit's own flow temperature. Without it the heat reaching that circuit cannot be told.
data_description.add_another: Tick to describe one more circuit after this one.

zones.title: VT zones
zones.description: Pick the Versatile Thermostat zones heated by this boiler. Zones not picked are ignored.

data_description.zones: Only VT climate entities are offered. The plugin reads them; with control and learning pauses on, it also pauses and resumes their SmartPI learning. A zone left out neither calls for heat nor is watched for frost. A zone built on the boiler's or gateway's own thermostat entity is refused: it would ask for heat whenever the flame burns.

data.closes_when_off: Closes when VT switches it off

data_description.circuit: The heating circuit this zone is on. The wrong circuit attributes the zone's heat to the wrong water.
data_description.emitter: Radiators, underfloor or convectors. Sets the EN 442 exponent of the emitter power and the curve's default shape; the wrong type skews both.
data_description.foreign_heat: A fireplace, stove or electric heater in this room, not the sun: a switch or binary sensor that is on while it heats, or a power sensor (a temperature sensor at the advanced level, where its threshold is set). Shown as foreign heat for the zone; with control, its learning is paused meanwhile.
data_description.reference_output_w: The emitters' output at their reference condition, in W. Only for an absolute output estimate; a wrong value only skews that estimate.
data_description.exponent: Overrides the EN 442 exponent of the emitter type. A wrong exponent skews the emitter power factor.
data_description.power_threshold: A power source counts as heating above this, in W. Default 100 W. Too low counts standby as heating; too high misses a small heater.
data_description.temperature_threshold: Needed for a temperature source: it counts as heating above this, in °C. Too low counts a cold stove as heating; too high misses it.
data_description.closes_when_off: Tick if this zone's valve or emitter closes whenever Versatile Thermostat switches the zone off, although VT does not report its opening (e.g. a radiator thermostat VT turns off). Frost protection then does not heat for this zone while VT keeps it off, and raises a repair issue instead. Off (default): the zone is heated in frost as before, which may run the boiler against a closed valve.

building.title: Building
building.description: A first estimate of your house's heat loss: rough answers are refined by recorded heating days. A value you enter always wins — the data never replace it; they show a mismatch. Leave empty what you do not know.

data_description.floor_area: In m². With the insulation class it gives a rough first estimate, shown until recorded days replace it; a rough estimate never decides the verdict.
data_description.insulation: Poor, average, good or very good. Part of the rough first estimate.
data_description.thermal_mass: How slowly the house cools. Recorded for later forecast features.
data_description.design_load_kw: Your own heat-loss calculation, in kW at the design outdoor temperature. Always wins: recorded days never replace it, they show a mismatch. A value no house has is refused.
data_description.loss_coefficient: Heat loss per kelvin, in kW/K, if you know it. Always wins, measured values included: recorded days never replace it, they show a mismatch — a wrong value stays wrong.
data_description.heating_threshold: Outdoor temperature above which the house needs no heating, in °C; also the degree-day base. Default 15 °C, until recorded days over a wide enough range of outdoor temperatures measure it. Entered, it always wins; the measured value is shown beside it with any mismatch. Wrong, degree-days and gas per degree-day are skewed.
data_description.design_outdoor: The coldest outdoor temperature your design load refers to, in °C. Default −15 °C. Wrong, the estimate from your design load is skewed.

reference.title: Reference room
reference.description: One room temperature and setpoint for controllers that need a single room.

data_description.strategy: Largest deficit follows the room furthest below its setpoint; a chosen zone always uses one room; average uses every heating room. It is only published for external controllers; a chosen zone that is away leaves them without a reference.
data_description.zone: Used with the chosen-zone strategy. A room that is often off or away leaves the reference unknown.
data_description.switch_margin: Another room must be this much colder before the reference switches, in K. Smaller follows faster but switches more often, which can disturb an external controller.

data_description.condensing_return: A return below this counts as condensing, in °C. Default 55 °C. Too high overstates the condensing share.
data_description.short_burn_min: Burns shorter than this count as short, in minutes. Default 10. Longer makes more burns short, and the verdict harsher.
data_description.monitoring_days: Days from when this integration was added before control can be switched on; the verdict needs this many days of data. Once they have passed, control may start even without a verdict — out of the heating season there may be too little data for one. Default 7; shorter is not allowed.
data_description.near_room_k: Water within this of the room counts as no hot water, in K. Default 3. Larger says 'no hot water' sooner.
data_description.foreign_heat_hold_min: How long a room still counts as warmed after its source stops, in minutes. Default 60. Longer keeps learning paused longer after a fire.
data_description.add_water_below: Optional: below this pressure you are told to add water, in bar — take it from your boiler's manual (its minimum operating pressure). Empty by default: no notification. It only informs; heating stops only while the boiler itself reports a fault that stops it. Too low tells you late; too high tells you while the pressure is fine.
data_description.pressure_high_warning: Pressure above this raises a warning, in bar. Default 2.5. Too high warns too late.
data_description.pressure_high_alarm: Pressure above this raises an alarm, in bar, and a notification after 5 minutes. Default 2.8, below your safety valve's rating, read on the valve (often 3 bar in Europe, about 2.1 bar / 30 psi in North America). Must be above the warning.
data_description.flue_gas_warning: Flue gas above this raises a warning on a condensing boiler, in °C. Default 85 °C. Too high warns too late.
data_description.flue_gas_alarm: Flue gas above this raises an alarm, in °C. Default 100 °C. A limit set too high warns too late for plastic flue pipes.
data_description.starts_per_hour_limit: More burner starts than this in an hour raise a warning. Default 12. Too high hides short-cycling.
data_description.unstable_burns_limit: More than this many burns under a minute in a day raise a warning. Default 10. Too high hides an ignition problem.
data_description.verdict_window_days: The verdict covers this many most recent days with data. Empty (default): every day kept, up to a year, filled at start from the recorder as far back as it reaches. Shorter follows a change in the house sooner; longer is steadier. It is never shorter than the monitoring period.

level.title: Level of detail
level.description: The level changes only what you see, never how the plugin behaves; switching it alone reloads nothing. With the defaults restored, saving reloads the integration: while control holds the boiler, it is handed back and taken again (a relay goes to its rest state and back).

data.restore_defaults: Restore advanced settings to their defaults

data_description.level: Simple shows the essentials; advanced shows every parameter.
data_description.restore_defaults: When switching to simple: tick to reset the advanced tuning — control's curve shape, limits and behaviour, the alarm reactions, the monitor's thresholds, the reference room's margin — to its defaults. Facts about your installation stay whatever you choose: mapped signals, the boiler, circuits, emitter sizes and values you entered — and the monitoring period and verdict window. Left unticked, the tuning stays active but hidden, and the options show that some advanced settings are active.

freshness.title: Freshness limits
freshness.description: An age limit per signal, in minutes: a value not reported for longer counts as stale, for the monitor and for control alike — without a fresh flame and flow, control writes nothing and hands back after five minutes. Empty (default): only whether the entity is available counts, since many sources (MQTT among them) report only on change and a steady value is not a stale one. Risk: without a limit, a source that freezes without going unavailable is not caught; a limit shorter than a source's reporting interval stops control in steady weather. Control reads the flame and the flow each by its own limit; a link that keeps dropping in and out counts as lost once it has been stale for five minutes within ten. The weather entity has its own limit, none by default. On an OpenTherm Gateway over MQTT, the gateway dropping off shows within about 90 s (its entities turn unavailable), but a broken link inside it, between its ESP and its PIC, may not be seen at all: its entities stay available and their values simply stop changing. Saving reloads the integration: while control holds the boiler, it is handed back and taken again (a relay goes to its rest state and back).

data_description.flame: Flame: its age limit, in minutes; a value not reported for longer counts as stale. Empty (default): only whether the entity is available counts. A limit shorter than the source's reporting interval makes a steady value stale. Control reads it by this limit: stale for five minutes within ten, the boiler is handed back.
data_description.flow: Flow temperature: its age limit, in minutes; a value not reported for longer counts as stale. Empty (default): only whether the entity is available counts. A limit shorter than the source's reporting interval makes a steady value stale. Control reads it by this limit: stale for five minutes within ten, the boiler is handed back.
data_description.return: Return temperature: its age limit, in minutes; a value not reported for longer counts as stale. Empty (default): only whether the entity is available counts. A limit shorter than the source's reporting interval makes a steady value stale.

data.class: What the boiler's integration can do

data_description.class: Flow setpoint, curve parameters only, on/off or read-only. Control (experimental): a flow setpoint (water temperature) or on/off (relay); the other classes are monitored only.
data_description.dhw: None, a storage tank or a combi boiler; required. Used to interpret burns: with "none" every burn counts as heating — declared on a boiler that heats hot water, its draws would count as heating starts; the wrong type counts hot water as heating or the reverse.
data_description.condensing: Condensing boilers get flue gas limits for condensing appliances and are judged on how often they condense; for other boilers the absolute flue gas alarm is off and condensing plays no part in the verdict. The wrong choice warns too late or for nothing, and misjudges the verdict.
data_description.boiler_min_power: Lowest heating power from the manual, in kW. Compared with the building load: a load often below it means the boiler must cycle. A wrong value skews that judgement in the verdict.
data_description.boiler_max_power: Highest heating power in kW. With the minimum and the modulation it estimates heat output; a wrong value skews heat and gas estimates.
data_description.max_ch_setpoint: Highest flow temperature in heating, in °C. Flow above it points to a DHW run; set too low, heating counts as hot water. Control never writes a setpoint above it either: set too low, rooms stay cold in hard frost.
data_description.gas_at_min_power: Gas per hour at minimum power, in your gas meter's unit. With the modulation it estimates gas use when there is no meter; a wrong value skews gas per degree-day.
data_description.gas_at_max_power: Gas per hour at maximum power, in the same unit; a wrong value skews the gas estimates.
data_description.modulation_scale: Whether 0 % is the minimum power (the OpenTherm definition) or the value is a percentage of maximum power. The wrong choice skews heat and gas estimates.
data_description.bypass: Tick when the heating water always has a path — an automatic bypass valve or a low-loss header: the low-flow warning is then off, as closed valves cannot stop the flow. Left unticked on such a system, the warning is false; ticked without one, a real dead-end goes unwarned.

circuit.title: Heating circuit {number}
circuit.description: How this circuit's water temperature is set. Saving reloads the integration: while control holds the boiler, it is handed back and taken again (a relay goes to its rest state and back).

data_description.control: Unmixed, straight from the boiler; mixed through the boiler (a second circuit the boiler mixes); mixed by a separate controller; or a thermostatic mixing valve (fixed). Control runs only for one circuit fed straight from the boiler, or through a fixed valve. The wrong type makes control refuse, or misjudge what reaches the rooms.
data_description.max_flow: The most this circuit may receive, in °C, e.g. underfloor heating on an unmixed loop: control never asks for more, but the boiler may overshoot it by its own hysteresis — set the alarm below to be told. Needed for underfloor on an unmixed loop. Too high overheats the floor.
data_description.fixed_temperature: Needed for a thermostatic mixing valve (fixed): its setting in °C. The boiler's water is kept at least 5 K above it, so the mixing valve can reach it; set higher than the valve's setting, the water runs hotter than needed.
data_description.max_flow_alarm: Information alarm when the measured flow stays above this, in °C. Starts at the maximum + 5 °C. Needs a flow reading. Too high lets a real overshoot pass unreported.
data_description.max_flow_alarm_min: How long, in minutes, before the alarm rises. Starts at 10. Too short reports every overshoot of the boiler's hysteresis.
data_description.flow_entity: A mixed circuit's own flow temperature. Without it the heat reaching that circuit cannot be told.
data_description.add_another: Tick to describe one more circuit after this one.

zones.title: VT zones
zones.description: Pick the Versatile Thermostat zones heated by this boiler. Zones not picked are ignored. Saving reloads the integration: while control holds the boiler, it is handed back and taken again (a relay goes to its rest state and back).

data_description.zones: Only VT climate entities are offered. The plugin reads them; with control and learning pauses on, it also pauses and resumes their SmartPI learning. A zone left out neither calls for heat nor is watched for frost. A zone built on the boiler's or gateway's own thermostat entity is refused: it would ask for heat whenever the flame burns.

zone.title: Zone {zone}
zone.description: How this zone is heated. Saving reloads the integration: while control holds the boiler, it is handed back and taken again (a relay goes to its rest state and back).

data.closes_when_off: Closes when VT switches it off

data_description.circuit: The heating circuit this zone is on. The wrong circuit attributes the zone's heat to the wrong water.
data_description.emitter: Radiators, underfloor or convectors. Sets the EN 442 exponent of the emitter power and the curve's default shape; the wrong type skews both.
data_description.foreign_heat: A fireplace, stove or electric heater in this room, not the sun: a switch or binary sensor that is on while it heats, or a power sensor (a temperature sensor at the advanced level, where its threshold is set). Shown as foreign heat for the zone; with control, its learning is paused meanwhile.
data_description.reference_output_w: The emitters' output at their reference condition, in W. Only for an absolute output estimate; a wrong value only skews that estimate.
data_description.exponent: Overrides the EN 442 exponent of the emitter type. A wrong exponent skews the emitter power factor.
data_description.power_threshold: A power source counts as heating above this, in W. Default 100 W. Too low counts standby as heating; too high misses a small heater.
data_description.temperature_threshold: Needed for a temperature source: it counts as heating above this, in °C. Too low counts a cold stove as heating; too high misses it.
data_description.closes_when_off: Tick if this zone's valve or emitter closes whenever Versatile Thermostat switches the zone off, although VT does not report its opening (e.g. a radiator thermostat VT turns off). Frost protection then does not heat for this zone while VT keeps it off, and raises a repair issue instead. Off (default): the zone is heated in frost as before, which may run the boiler against a closed valve.

building.title: Building
building.description: A first estimate of your house's heat loss: rough answers are refined by recorded heating days. A value you enter always wins — the data never replace it; they show a mismatch. Leave empty what you do not know. Saving reloads the integration: while control holds the boiler, it is handed back and taken again (a relay goes to its rest state and back).

data_description.floor_area: In m². With the insulation class it gives a rough first estimate, shown until recorded days replace it; a rough estimate never decides the verdict.
data_description.insulation: Poor, average, good or very good. Part of the rough first estimate.
data_description.thermal_mass: How slowly the house cools. Recorded for later forecast features.
data_description.design_load_kw: Your own heat-loss calculation, in kW at the design outdoor temperature. Always wins: recorded days never replace it, they show a mismatch. A value no house has is refused.
data_description.loss_coefficient: Heat loss per kelvin, in kW/K, if you know it. Always wins, measured values included: recorded days never replace it, they show a mismatch — a wrong value stays wrong.
data_description.heating_threshold: Outdoor temperature above which the house needs no heating, in °C; also the degree-day base. Default 15 °C, until recorded days over a wide enough range of outdoor temperatures measure it. Entered, it always wins; the measured value is shown beside it with any mismatch. Wrong, degree-days and gas per degree-day are skewed.
data_description.design_outdoor: The coldest outdoor temperature your design load refers to, in °C. Default −15 °C. Wrong, the estimate from your design load is skewed.

reference.title: Reference room
reference.description: One room temperature and setpoint for controllers that need a single room. Saving reloads the integration: while control holds the boiler, it is handed back and taken again (a relay goes to its rest state and back).

data_description.strategy: Largest deficit follows the room furthest below its setpoint; a chosen zone always uses one room; average uses every heating room. It is only published for external controllers; a chosen zone that is away leaves them without a reference.
data_description.zone: Used with the chosen-zone strategy. A room that is often off or away leaves the reference unknown.
data_description.switch_margin: Another room must be this much colder before the reference switches, in K. Smaller follows faster but switches more often, which can disturb an external controller.

monitor.title: Monitor
monitor.description: Thresholds of the analysis. Saving reloads the integration: while control holds the boiler, it is handed back and taken again (a relay goes to its rest state and back).

data_description.condensing_return: A return below this counts as condensing, in °C. Default 55 °C. Too high overstates the condensing share.
data_description.short_burn_min: Burns shorter than this count as short, in minutes. Default 10. Longer makes more burns short, and the verdict harsher.
data_description.monitoring_days: Days from when this integration was added before control can be switched on; the verdict needs this many days of data. Once they have passed, control may start even without a verdict — out of the heating season there may be too little data for one. Default 7; shorter is not allowed.
data_description.near_room_k: Water within this of the room counts as no hot water, in K. Default 3. Larger says 'no hot water' sooner.
data_description.foreign_heat_hold_min: How long a room still counts as warmed after its source stops, in minutes. Default 60. Longer keeps learning paused longer after a fire.
data_description.add_water_below: Optional: below this pressure you are told to add water, in bar — take it from your boiler's manual (its minimum operating pressure). Empty by default: no notification. It only informs; heating stops only while the boiler itself reports a fault that stops it. Too low tells you late; too high tells you while the pressure is fine.
data_description.pressure_high_warning: Pressure above this raises a warning, in bar. Default 2.5. Too high warns too late.
data_description.pressure_high_alarm: Pressure above this raises an alarm, in bar, and a notification after 5 minutes. Default 2.8, below your safety valve's rating, read on the valve (often 3 bar in Europe, about 2.1 bar / 30 psi in North America). Must be above the warning.
data_description.flue_gas_warning: Flue gas above this raises a warning on a condensing boiler, in °C. Default 85 °C. Too high warns too late.
data_description.flue_gas_alarm: Flue gas above this raises an alarm, in °C. Default 100 °C. A limit set too high warns too late for plastic flue pipes.
data_description.starts_per_hour_limit: More burner starts than this in an hour raise a warning. Default 12. Too high hides short-cycling.
data_description.unstable_burns_limit: More than this many burns under a minute in a day raise a warning. Default 10. Too high hides an ignition problem.
data_description.verdict_window_days: The verdict covers this many most recent days with data. Empty (default): every day kept, up to a year, filled at start from the recorder as far back as it reaches. Shorter follows a change in the house sooner; longer is steadier. It is never shorter than the monitoring period.

control.title: Control (experimental)
control.description: How the plugin controls the boiler: the flow setpoint it writes, or on and off through a relay. Control stays off until you switch it on, and only after the monitoring period, counted in days from when this integration was added. Control may then start even without a verdict — out of the heating season the monitor may have too little data for one; the control switch shows the verdict. Choose "No control" to keep monitoring only. Saving reloads the integration: while control holds the boiler, it is handed back and taken again (a relay goes to its rest state and back).

data.thermostat_kind: What is wired to the gateway's thermostat terminals

data_description.write_path: No control (default); a writable entity you pick, e.g. an EMS-ESP or ESPHome OpenTherm number; the OpenTherm Gateway through Home Assistant's OpenTherm Gateway integration; or the OTGW firmware's MQTT commands. Pick the path your boiler interface really offers: a wrong one means writes that fail or go nowhere. A relay, for an on/off boiler: a switch on the boiler's room-thermostat terminals, or a boiler thermostat entity set to heat or off. Only the paths that suit the boiler class are offered.
data_description.topology: How the gateway sits between thermostat and boiler. With a thermostat: on hand-back the thermostat takes over. Stand-alone, without a thermostat: on hand-back, and whenever Home Assistant stops for more than about a minute, the boiler stops heating. Monitor mode: the gateway only listens and control is not possible. Virtual: a controller on the Home Assistant side, e.g. ESPHome, drives the boiler. Required; declare it as it is — the plugin never changes the gateway's mode. A lost link to the boiler's data raises an alarm and hands back in every topology — stand-alone, heating stops until the data returns. With a thermostat: while the plugin controls, the wall thermostat's heating setting and its off switch do nothing — its hot-water settings still work; after a hand-back, or while Home Assistant is down, it heats by its own setting and program, so keep them at what the house should get. Not used with a relay: its state after hand-back is what a hand-back does.
data_description.thermostat_kind: Only for a gateway, with a thermostat or stand-alone. OpenTherm thermostat: it talks to the boiler and may show the water temperature. On/off contact: a simple thermostat or switch on two wires — the gateway turns it into a heating request, and the plugin's "heating off" would block it after a Home Assistant crash, so control is not offered. Nothing: no thermostat at all. I don't know: control is not offered until you check. With a thermostat pick OpenTherm; stand-alone pick Nothing.
data_description.confirmed_entity: The entity that reports the setpoint the boiler received, e.g. the gateway's "Control setpoint 1" on its boiler device — it shows what the gateway sends, so the setpoint is shown as confirmed by the gateway, not by the boiler. Required: every write is checked against it, and a write the boiler ignores or another controller overwrites is reported. The plugin's setpoint entity shows only a confirmed value, otherwise unknown. Picking the entity you write confirms nothing: the setpoint is then shown as unverified. Not used with a relay: its own state confirms it.
data_description.ch_confirmed_entity: Optional: an entity that reports whether the boiler receives heating enabled — e.g. the gateway's "Central heating 1" on its boiler device that reads On/Off: what the gateway sends. Not the one that reads Running/Not running: that is the boiler's own status, which goes off during hot water and would look like another controller. With it, heating on/off is checked like the setpoint: a switch the boiler ignores is reported, and one another controller changes is written again once, then every write stops. Without it, heating on/off is shown as unverified and another controller switching it goes unnoticed. Picking the entity you write, or the thermostat's request instead of what the boiler receives, confirms nothing or stops control. Pick an entity that reports a change within about a minute: a slower one delays noticing a change, and one slower than 5 min can make the plugin wrongly step aside.
data_description.thermostat_setpoint_entity: Optional, for a gateway with an OpenTherm thermostat: the water temperature the thermostat itself asks for (with opentherm_gw, the thermostat device's "Control setpoint 1"), not the boiler's read-back. When the boiler falls back to it after an outage, the plugin sends its command again instead of taking it for another controller. It also shows the hand-back as done when the gateway passes the thermostat's request on — the OTGW firmware over MQTT then never shows 0, so without this field a hand-back to a thermostat asking for the lowest water temperature or the plugin's last value is never confirmed. Empty (default): only the value from before the plugin counts.
data_description.restart_entity: Optional: a sensor of the gateway or boiler interface that shows its restarts — an uptime that starts again from a low value, a restart counter that goes up, or a boot time (for example the OTGW firmware's reboot count, or an EMS-ESP or ESPHome uptime sensor). A restart it shows counts for 5 minutes as a trace of an outage: the boiler falling back to its own value then is taken as a lost command and simply sent again. Empty (default): a restart is seen only when the device's entities go unavailable, and a quick restart that shows nothing is judged as a fall-back without a trace — the first within an hour is still sent again, but a second may be taken for another controller, and the plugin steps aside.

control_entity.title: Writable entity
control_entity.description: The entity that takes the flow setpoint, and how control is handed back. Saving reloads the integration: while control holds the boiler, it is handed back and taken again (a relay goes to its rest state and back).

data.own_room_controller: The boiler has its own room controller

data_description.setpoint_entity: A number or input_number that sets the boiler's flow temperature.
data_description.write_type: Expiring: the device drops the value unless it is repeated; it is repeated every 30 s. Held: written on change, and again every 5 minutes and when the device returns. Persistent or unknown (default): stored in the boiler's memory, or it may be — the plugin never writes to the boiler's persistent memory, so control is not available with such an entity. Risk: a stored parameter declared expiring would be written every 30 s, about 2,900 times a day, and wear the boiler's memory out. Held: the device keeps the last value it was given (ESPHome, DIYLess and the like). EMS-ESP's flow setpoint (selflowtemp) is not held — it expires within about a minute — so declare it expiring. Held: risks — a boiler parameter kept in its memory but declared held is written at every change and every 5 minutes, and wears the memory (e.g. EMS-ESP's heating temperature parameter); and the last held value, "off" included, stays on the boiler while Home Assistant is down.
data_description.ch_entity: A switch that turns heating on and off — needed for control in this version: without it, "off" would be a low setpoint, and whether that stops the boiler and its pump is not known yet, so control stays blocked and only the monitor runs. It is turned back on at hand-back where the boiler returns to its own control or a thermostat, and left as it is where the hand-back stops heating; its write type is needed below. It must not be the external control switch. Never pick a switch that is stored in the boiler's memory (e.g. a boiler's "heating activated" parameter): every switching would wear it. On must allow heating: a flag that stops heating while on (such as EMS-ESP's "heating off") turns every command round and must not be used here.
data_description.ch_write_type: Needed with a heating switch: what the device does with its state. Expiring: dropped unless repeated; repeated every 30 s. Held: written on change, and again every 5 minutes and when the device returns. The plugin never writes to the boiler's persistent memory, so a switch declared persistent or unknown is refused. Held: the device keeps the last value it was given (ESPHome, DIYLess and the like). EMS-ESP's flow setpoint (selflowtemp) is not held — it expires within about a minute — so declare it expiring. Held: risks — a boiler parameter kept in its memory but declared held is written at every change and every 5 minutes, and wears the memory (e.g. EMS-ESP's heating temperature parameter); and the last held value, "off" included, stays on the boiler while Home Assistant is down.
data_description.hand_back: How control returns to the boiler on every exit. Every hand-back first writes the lowest water temperature, then turns the heating switch back on where the boiler returns to its own control or a thermostat, then follows the method chosen here: write a hand-back value; stop writing and let the device's own timeout take over, for expiring writes only; or turn off a switch that enables external control. Required; control cannot be switched on without it.
data_description.hand_back_value: The setpoint written on hand-back, in °C, for the value method: the value that returns the boiler to its own control, or the one it should keep. 0 means "own control" on some devices and "no heat" on others. Required for the value method. It must not exceed the highest water temperature or the circuit's maximum, and is never cut down to them; it counts as done once the read-back shows it.
data_description.hand_back_value_effect: Required with the value method: what the device does with the hand-back value — its own control resumes, or heating stops. The control switch shows it as what hand-back leads to.
data_description.hand_back_entity: For the switch method: the switch that enables external control. It is turned on when control starts and off on hand-back — so never a setting the device stores in its memory; its write type is needed below.
data_description.hand_back_entity_write_type: Needed with the switch method: what the device does with the switch's state. Expiring: dropped unless repeated — turned on again every 30 s while control holds the boiler. Held: the device keeps it — turned on each time control takes the boiler, and again every 5 minutes and when the device returns. Persistent or unknown (default): it may be stored in the boiler's memory, which every switching would wear, so control is not available with it.
data_description.hand_back_timeout_min: For the timeout method: how long, in minutes, the device keeps the last value it was given before it returns to its own control — take it from the device's documentation (1 to 60; default 1, EMS-ESP's flow setpoint lapses within about a minute). Every hand-back writes the lowest water temperature first, so the boiler stays at it for this long. The hand-back is judged only after it — back at the value from before control, or at a value of the device's own — and "hand-back failed" comes 3 minutes after it. Too short: a false alarm while the device still holds the lowest; too long: a device that never lets go is reported late. Not used with the other methods.
data_description.own_room_controller: Tick only if the boiler has a room controller of its own that asks for heat by itself once the plugin lets go — for example a room unit on the boiler's bus (EMS). If Versatile Thermostat gives no answer at all, the plugin then hands the boiler back to it; without the tick the boiler does not heat, and an alarm and a repair notice tell you why. Every other hand-back also goes to that controller. With a relay it counts only when the relay's state after hand-back is "on"; with "off", the boiler does not heat when Versatile Thermostat gives no answer. Off by default. Risk: without such a controller, the boiler would be left on its own dial, heating with no room in charge.

control_gateway.title: OpenTherm Gateway
control_gateway.description: The gateway set up in Home Assistant's OpenTherm Gateway integration. Saving reloads the integration: while control holds the boiler, it is handed back and taken again (a relay goes to its rest state and back).

data_description.gateway_id: The gateway set up in the OpenTherm Gateway integration; only gateways set up and enabled there are offered. The control setpoint is repeated every 30 s; on hand-back it is set to 0, which returns control to the thermostat, or ends heating without one. Heating on/off (CH=) is kept by the gateway until it changes or the gateway restarts; the plugin sends it again with the control setpoint, every 30 s, and when the gateway returns.

control_mqtt.title: OTGW firmware over MQTT
control_mqtt.description: Commands are published on the topic prefix/set/node/command, with the prefix and node name given below. Heating on/off (CH=) is kept by the gateway until it changes or the gateway restarts; the plugin sends it again with the control setpoint, every 30 s, and when the gateway returns. Saving reloads the integration: while control holds the boiler, it is handed back and taken again (a relay goes to its rest state and back).

data_description.mqtt_top: The MQTT topic prefix set in the OTGW firmware. Default OTGW.
data_description.mqtt_node: The node name set in the OTGW firmware. A wrong prefix or node name sends commands nowhere; the read-back then reports them as ignored.

control_curve.title: Heating curve and limits
control_curve.description: The flow temperature the house needs at each outdoor temperature, the limits no setpoint may pass, and how long heating waits for slow valves. Saving reloads the integration: while control holds the boiler, it is handed back and taken again (a relay goes to its rest state and back).

data_description.design_outdoor: The coldest outdoor temperature your heating is designed for, in °C. Default: the building's design outdoor temperature, or −15 °C. Too cold a value gives too little water in frost.
data_description.design_flow: The flow temperature the heating needs at the design outdoor temperature, in °C, e.g. the value on your boiler's own curve. Required; there is no default. Too high wastes gas and makes the burner cycle; too low leaves rooms cold in hard frost.
data_description.hard_min: The lowest water temperature the plugin sets, in °C, set like a point of the curve. Default 20 °C. Too low: in mild weather the boiler stops by itself again and again, and a boiler that is not condensing condenses in its flue — take the value from its manual. Too high: water warmer than the rooms need, and more gas. When the boiler keeps stopping at this temperature, the plugin shows its evidence and a suggested value; it never changes this setting itself.
data_description.hard_max: No setpoint above this, whatever the curve or a correction asks, in °C. Default 70 °C. Underfloor heating also needs its circuit's maximum flow.
data_description.activation_delay_s: Seconds heating waits after the first call for heat, so slow valves (thermoelectric, underfloor) open before the boiler and its pump run — as Versatile Thermostat's central boiler did; pre-filled from VT's own setting where VT kept one. Stopping is never delayed. Default 0: at once. Risk: a zone whose heating pulse is shorter than the delay never starts the boiler, and pulses close to it give short burns; without a heating switch ("off" as a low setpoint) the pump may run anyway.
data_description.room: The room temperature the curve is built for, in °C. Default 20 °C. Too high raises the whole curve and wastes gas.
data_description.exponent: How the curve bends. Empty picks it from the emitters: radiators 1.3, convectors 1.4, underfloor 1.1. The wrong bend under-heats in frost or overheats in mild weather.
data_description.offset: Shifts the whole curve up or down, in K. Default 0. Up wastes gas; down leaves rooms cold.
data_description.ceiling_band: How far above the curve the comfort correction may raise the water, in K. The correction stops at 3 K on its own: a band of 3 K or more leaves it that bound, a smaller one lowers it, and 0 turns correction off in effect. Default 10 K. Risk: a small band gives a room that stays cold less help.
data_description.fallback_setpoint: Used when no outdoor temperature is known — the sensor failed, or the monitor found it stuck or far from the weather, and the weather entity is missing too — once the last effective temperature has been held for three hours, in °C. Empty (default): the curve at its design point, the most heat the curve gives: never too little heat, the valves keep rooms from overheating.
data_description.frost_limit: A watched zone colder than this starts heating, whatever else applies, where heat can reach it — its valve open or its device on — in °C. Default 5 °C. Too low risks frozen pipes; too high heats rooms you keep off.
data_description.frost_release: Frost protection ends once every watched zone is above this, in °C. Default 7 °C, above the limit. Close to the limit, frost heating starts and stops more often.
data_description.frost_zone: Optional: watch only this zone for frost. Empty (default): every zone. Frost heating runs only for a cold room whose valve can open — Versatile Thermostat reports it open or its device on; a cold room VT keeps closed raises a repair issue instead. Frost heating that does not warm the room for two hours raises an alarm; it is never stopped.

control_behaviour.title: Control behaviour
control_behaviour.description: The ramp, the decision interval, the "off" setpoint, demand thresholds and learning pauses. Heating goes on and off with Versatile Thermostat's zones, at once: nothing counted or timed holds it. Every default is the cautious one. Saving reloads the integration: while control holds the boiler, it is handed back and taken again (a relay goes to its rest state and back).

data_description.ramp_k_per_min: The fastest setpoint change, in K per minute. Default 1. Faster changes stress the boiler and make zones overshoot.
data_description.decision_interval_min: How often the water temperature is decided anew, in minutes; default 5, VT's default cycle. Heating on and off follows the zones at every 10 s step, whatever this is; the plugin does not read the zones' own cycles. Shorter: the water follows the weather and the rooms sooner, but the zones' algorithms see it move more often; longer: steadier water that follows more slowly.
data_description.off_setpoint: The setpoint written for "off" when there is no heating switch, in °C. Default 10: far below any heating value, and below the lowest water temperature. Risk: a low setpoint does not switch the boiler's heating off — ESPHome and DIYLess masters keep CH enabled, and boilers are reported to keep their CH pump running; a heating switch, or an OpenTherm Gateway's CH=0, really turns heating off. Control without a heating switch is blocked in this version, so this setpoint is not written yet.
data_description.count_threshold: Heating is needed when at least this many zones call for heat. Default 1; at most the number of zones. 0 turns the count off, leaving the power or opening threshold alone, as in Versatile Thermostat — then every zone must report what that threshold needs, or its room could never ask for heat: the form refuses a zone that does not, and a calling zone that does not raises the "demand criterion has no data" alarm. Higher leaves a single calling room without heat.
data_description.power_threshold_kw: Optional: heating is needed when the zones' mean power over their cycle, as Versatile Thermostat counts it, reaches this, in kW — counted only while at least one of them has its valve open or its device on. A zone without a device power set in VT gives it no data; with a zone count of 0 such a zone could never ask for heat. Too high leaves small rooms without heat.
data_description.opening_threshold: Optional: heating is needed when the widest valve opening among the calling zones reaches this, in %. A zone without a valve opening or duty cycle (VT's over_climate) gives it no data; with a zone count of 0 such a zone could never ask for heat. Too high leaves a room that opens a little without heat.
data_description.learning_pauses: Pause SmartPI learning while hot water runs, while foreign heat warms a zone and while the water temperature swings, so it does not learn what the boiler did; each pause and resume is read back from SmartPI. After hot water it waits for the water to come back, at most an hour after the draw; after foreign heat or a swing, only the minimum pause. Default on. Auto-TPI cannot be paused without resetting what it learned, so zones running it are reported instead. Off: SmartPI learns through those moments too, which can skew its model.
data_description.comfort_correction: Off (default): the water follows the curve alone. Recommended: the relay contact on the boiler's room-thermostat terminals — a volt-free contact; check the manual or ask an installer, as these terminals may carry mains voltage — never in the boiler's power supply, which would also cut its pump overrun and its own frost protection. data_description.relay_entity: The switch on the boiler's room-thermostat terminals, or a boiler thermostat entity the plugin sets to heat or off. Not a helper (input_boolean): it confirms nothing. Never a setting the boiler stores in its memory (e.g. EMS-ESP's "heating activated"): every switching would wear it. Not a switch a Versatile Thermostat zone uses. For a boiler thermostat entity, "heat" confirms the command, not that the burner fires. A Zigbee relay may look available for up to 2 hours after it dies (ZHA), or always (Zigbee2MQTT with availability off): turn availability reporting on.
data_description.relay_is_separate_contact: Tick to confirm that the relay is a separate contact (e.g. on the boiler's room-thermostat terminals), not an on/off setting the boiler keeps in its memory, such as EMS-ESP's "heating activated": every switching would wear that memory. Control does not start until this is ticked.
data_description.relay_reports_state: Yes: the relay sends its contact state to Home Assistant; the plugin checks it every 5 minutes and after every return, writes only when it differs, sends its command again after a restart (up to 3 unreported restarts a day), and sets it back once if something else switches it; a second switch within a day, or a fourth unreported restart, makes the plugin set the relay to its state after hand-back once, step aside and leave it alone. No, or I don't know (default): the plugin cannot see the relay, repeats its command at the repeat interval and shows "controlled without confirmation"; a change made at the relay is undone within that time. An entity marked as an assumed state always counts as no.
data_description.relay_power_on_state: What the relay does when its power returns — its own setting, which the plugin cannot read. Off (recommended): the boiler waits off until Home Assistant is back and gives its command. On, last state, or I don't know (default): after a power cut the boiler may heat without control until Home Assistant is back. Off or On: a relay found in that state, although Home Assistant saw no outage, is taken as restarted, and the plugin sends its command again — up to 3 times a day; the fourth time counts as something else switching the relay, and the plugin steps aside. Last state or I don't know: any change at the relay is taken as a possible restart in the same way.
data_description.relay_off_timer: Whether the relay switches itself off some time after an "on" (Tasmota's PulseTime; a Shelly's auto-off — whether a Shelly restarts it on a repeated "on" is not documented, so test it). None: the plugin writes only when the relay's state differs. A length (enter it below): the plugin repeats "on" at half that time, at most at the repeat interval, and the relay switches heating off by itself if Home Assistant stops; a switch-off within a minute of that length after "on" — or of twice or three times it — is the timer's and is answered with "on", while any other switch-off counts as the relay being switched by something else. I don't know (default): treated as "it may have one" — the plugin repeats "on" at the repeat interval. A switch-off at least that interval after the relay went on is answered with "on". When switch-offs keep coming the same time after "on" — 9 min or more (a 10-min timer measured up to a minute short) — the plugin takes them for the relay's own timer: it goes on answering them, no longer counts them, and asks you to declare the timer; shorter ones keep counting, as each starts the boiler again. Any other switch-off counts like a restart the relay did not report: the fourth within a day makes the plugin step aside, as it cannot be told from an automation or a person switching the relay; a timer shorter than that interval looks like something else switching the relay. So if the relay has a timer, declare its length. Set a timer in the relay only once the plugin's control starts, or it switches heating off while VT still drives the relay.
data_description.relay_off_timer_min: Only with a length above: the minutes, 10–120, after which the relay switches itself off — exactly as set in the relay: a switch-off more than a minute away from it, or from twice or three times it, counts as the relay being switched by something else, and the plugin steps aside at the fourth within a day. A shorter timer is not accepted: each time it ran out, the boiler would start again.
data_description.relay_repeat_s: For a relay that reports no state, or has or may have its own timer: how often the plugin repeats its command, in seconds, 10–300. Empty (default): 300 s. Filled in from Versatile Thermostat's keep-alive when it had one of at most 300 s; a longer one is not filled in. At most 300 s: a relay that restarted in the wrong state stays so at most this long. Some relays store every command, so shorter is not always better.
data_description.relay_rest_state: What the relay is set to whenever the plugin gives control back (control switched off, an error, a Home Assistant stop, or stepping aside from another controller). Off (default): the boiler heats only through a thermostat wired in parallel, if there is one; without one heating stops, and the plugin tells you when a room asks for heat or is near freezing. On: the boiler heats by its own setting with no room control — rooms are limited only by their valves, and the boiler may run against closed valves; choose it only for a boiler meant to run so, e.g. one delivered with a jumper on these terminals or with a thermostat wired in series.
data_description.own_room_controller: Tick only if the boiler has a room controller of its own that asks for heat by itself once the plugin lets go, and the relay's state after hand-back is "on" — the relay is then the boiler's heat-demand contact. If Versatile Thermostat gives no answer at all, the plugin then hands the relay back to "on", and that controller heats. With the state after hand-back "off" the tick changes nothing: when Versatile Thermostat gives no answer, the relay stays off, with an alarm. Off by default. Risk: without such a controller, a relay handed back "on" leaves the boiler heating with no room in charge.
data_description.boiler_heats_above_w: Optional, with the boiler's electric power mapped: the power in W above which the boiler counts as heating. Empty (default): the power is not used as proof.

control_relay_behaviour.title: Relay: when it switches
control_relay_behaviour.description: The relay switches the boiler on and off with Versatile Thermostat's zones and frost protection, at once — after VT's activation delay for a start; nothing counted or timed holds it, as in VT's own central boiler. Every default is the cautious one. Saving reloads the integration: while control holds the boiler, it is handed back and taken again (a relay goes to its rest state and back).

data_description.activation_delay_s: Seconds heating waits after the first call for heat, so slow valves (thermoelectric, underfloor) open before the boiler and its pump run — as Versatile Thermostat's central boiler did; pre-filled from VT's own setting where VT kept one, for you to confirm. Stopping is never delayed. Default 0: at once. Risk: a zone whose heating pulse is shorter than the delay never starts the boiler, and pulses close to it give short burns.
data_description.count_threshold: Heating is needed when at least this many zones call for heat. Default 1; at most the number of zones. 0 turns the count off, leaving the power or opening threshold alone, as in Versatile Thermostat — then every zone must report what that threshold needs, or its room could never ask for heat: the form refuses a zone that does not, and a calling zone that does not raises the "demand criterion has no data" alarm. Higher leaves a single calling room without heat.
data_description.power_threshold_kw: Optional: heating is needed when the zones' mean power over their cycle, as Versatile Thermostat counts it, reaches this, in kW — counted only while at least one of them has its valve open or its device on. A zone without a device power set in VT gives it no data; with a zone count of 0 such a zone could never ask for heat. Too high leaves small rooms without heat.
data_description.opening_threshold: Optional: heating is needed when the widest valve opening among the calling zones reaches this, in %. A zone without a valve opening or duty cycle (VT's over_climate) gives it no data; with a zone count of 0 such a zone could never ask for heat. Too high leaves a room that opens a little without heat.
data_description.learning_pauses: Pause SmartPI learning while hot water runs and while foreign heat warms a zone, so it does not learn what the boiler did; each pause and resume is read back from SmartPI. With a relay the boiler sets its own water temperature, so its swings pause nothing. Default on. Auto-TPI cannot be paused without resetting what it learned, so zones running it are reported instead. Off: SmartPI learns through those moments too, which can skew its model.
data_description.frost_limit: A watched zone colder than this starts heating, whatever else applies, where heat can reach it — its valve open or its device on — in °C. Default 5 °C. Too low risks frozen pipes; too high heats rooms you keep off.
data_description.frost_release: Frost protection ends once every watched zone is above this, in °C. Default 7 °C, above the limit. Close to the limit, frost heating starts and stops more often.
data_description.frost_zone: Optional: watch only this zone for frost. Empty (default): every zone. Frost heating runs only for a cold room whose valve can open — Versatile Thermostat reports it open or its device on; a cold room VT keeps closed raises a repair issue instead. Frost heating that does not warm the room for two hours raises an alarm; it is never stopped.

blocked_heating_on_ignored.message: From the start of the session the boiler did not take the plugin's "heating on" — or the relay its "on" — so the plugin could not make the boiler heat. The monitor keeps running. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_relay_off_not_taken.message: The relay took the plugin's commands earlier in the session, then did not show "off" for about 15 minutes, so the plugin could not switch heating off — the boiler may keep heating. Check the relay, its connection and the entity picked in the options, then switch control off and on. The monitor keeps running. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).
