blocked_mqtt_not_set_up.message: The MQTT integration is removed or disabled: the commands would go nowhere. Set it up or enable it. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_zone_not_vt.message: A zone is not a Versatile Thermostat thermostat, and only those can be zones: remove it in the options. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_zone_on_boiler_thermostat.message: A Versatile Thermostat zone is built on the boiler's or gateway's own thermostat entity: it would ask for heat whenever the flame burns. Build the zone on a room sensor and its valves or radiator thermostats instead. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_design_flow_too_low.message: The design flow temperature must be at least 5 K above the curve's room temperature. Correct it in the options. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_design_flow_above_hard_max.message: The design flow temperature is above the highest water temperature, so the curve would be cut off in frost. Raise the highest water temperature or lower the design flow in the options. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_design_outdoor_too_warm.message: The design outdoor temperature must be at least 10 K below the curve's room temperature. Correct it in the options. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_hard_min_not_below_design_flow.message: The lowest water temperature must be below the design flow temperature. Correct it in the options. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_hard_min_above_max.message: The lowest water temperature is above the circuit's or the boiler's maximum: the hand-back would first send the boiler hotter water than they allow. Lower it in the options. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_thermostat_on_off.message: An on/off contact is wired to the gateway's thermostat terminals: the gateway's "heating off" would block it after a Home Assistant crash, so control is not offered. The monitor keeps running. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_thermostat_kind_unknown.message: Control waits until you say, in the control options, what is wired to the gateway's thermostat terminals. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_thermostat_kind_contradicts_topo.message: This answer does not fit the gateway connection: an OpenTherm thermostat means "Gateway with a thermostat", nothing means stand-alone. Pick the other connection. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_boiler_class_no_control.message: Control needs a boiler of the class "Flow setpoint" or "On/off (relay)". Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_path_not_for_boiler_class.message: The write path does not suit the boiler class: a relay for an on/off boiler, a setpoint path for a flow-setpoint boiler. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_no_relay_entity.message: Pick the relay in the control options. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_relay_contact_not_confirmed.message: Control waits until you confirm, in the relay options, that the relay is a separate contact and not a setting stored in the boiler's memory. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_relay_domain_not_supported.message: The relay must be a switch or a boiler thermostat entity, not a helper. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_relay_climate_modes.message: This thermostat entity cannot be set to both heat and off. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_relay_used_by_zone.message: A Versatile Thermostat zone already switches this entity. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_relay_of_boiler_interface.message: This entity belongs to the boiler's or VT's own integration, not to a relay. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_relay_in_another_role.message: The relay is an entity the options already use in another role or as a signal. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_no_flame_signal.message: Water-temperature control needs the flame mapped in the signals. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

blocked_no_flow_signal.message: Water-temperature control needs the flow temperature mapped in the signals. Other reasons: {count} (all are listed on the control state).

auto_tpi_blocked.title: Auto-TPI cannot learn in some zones
auto_tpi_blocked.description: These zones run Auto-TPI and are marked in Versatile Thermostat as used by the central boiler, but VT's central boiler is not configured — the plugin replaces it — so Auto-TPI skips learning in them: {zones}. To let it learn, clear "used by the central boiler" in each zone's VT configuration. What that costs: the plugin cannot pause Auto-TPI without wiping what it has learned, so it will then also learn while hot water charges and while the water temperature changes, which can skew its coefficients. Leaving the option set keeps Auto-TPI's learning off in these zones.

hand_back_owed.title: Handing the boiler back has not got through

confirm.title: Handing the boiler back has not got through
confirm.description:
The plugin cannot hand the boiler back: its setpoint entity, heating switch or gateway does not take it. It retries every minute; until it gets through, the boiler may keep the last value the plugin wrote. Check that the device is available.

If you have returned the boiler to its own control by hand — or the device is gone for good — confirm here: the plugin stops retrying and forgets what it owed, and the options accept another device. Confirm only once the boiler really runs on its own.

control_options_invalid.title: The control options cannot be used
control_options_invalid.description: The saved control options cannot be used, so control is off; the monitor keeps running. The log names the option; open the options and set control up again.

control_state_unreadable.title: The plugin's memory of the boiler could not be read
control_state_unreadable.description: The file in which the plugin remembers whether it holds the boiler could not be read: it is missing or damaged (Home Assistant may show its own notice about a damaged file). To be safe, the plugin assumed it held the boiler and handed it back first. Control then works as usual; check that the boiler and the control switch are as you expect.

setup_failed_not_heated.title: The plugin did not start: the house is not heated
setup_failed_not_heated.description: The plugin could not start, so it does not control the boiler, and here handing the boiler back stops heating (a gateway without a thermostat, a hand-back value declared to stop heating, or a relay resting "off"): the house is not heated unless something else heats it. Only the boiler's own frost protection, if it has one, still works. Open Settings → Devices & services, find the plugin's entry and read its error; fix what it names, then reload the entry. This notice goes once the plugin starts.

setup_failed_may_not_be_heated.title: The plugin did not start: the house may not be heated
setup_failed_may_not_be_heated.description: The plugin could not start, so it does not control the boiler. Neither its options nor the options it took the boiler with can be read, so it cannot tell what the boiler does without it: where handing the boiler back stops heating (a gateway without a thermostat, a hand-back value declared to stop heating, or a relay resting "off"), the house is not heated. Open Settings → Devices & services, find the plugin's entry and read its error; fix what it names, then reload the entry. This notice goes once the plugin starts.

control_state_not_saved.title: The plugin cannot save its memory of the boiler
control_state_not_saved.description: Writing the file in which the plugin remembers whether it holds the boiler failed — a full disk, or a storage that turned read-only (Home Assistant's log has the error). A restart could then forget that the boiler holds a value the plugin wrote, so control does not take the boiler meanwhile: it handed it back, and a hand-back already owed is still made. Where a thermostat or the boiler's own control takes over, it heats now; where a hand-back stops heating, the boiler does not heat until control resumes. The plugin saves again every minute, and control resumes on its own once saving has worked for {minutes} minutes without a failure. Check Home Assistant's storage: its free space, and whether its disk or SD card is failing.

hand_back_owed_after_removal.title: The boiler may still hold a value from VTherm Smart Boiler
hand_back_owed_after_removal.description: The integration was removed before its hand-back reached the boiler. Return the boiler to its own control by hand — reset the setpoint entity, or clear the gateway's overrides — and then ignore this issue.

learning_not_paused.title: The plugin cannot pause learning in some zones
learning_not_paused.description: Control pauses zone learning while hot water charges, while foreign heat warms a zone and while the water temperature swings, but it cannot pause these zones: {zones}. Auto-TPI could only be paused by resetting what it learned, so the plugin leaves it alone; a SmartPI that does not publish its learning flag cannot be paused either. They keep learning through those moments, which can skew what they learn. To avoid it, stop Auto-TPI's learning in VT once it has learned, or update SmartPI — either leaves the zone without the plugin's protection until then.

vt_feature_manager_unsupported.title: VT's thermostats cannot show the plugin's zone values
vt_feature_manager_unsupported.description: The Versatile Thermostat installed here cannot load the plugin's feature manager (feature managers need VT {version} or newer, with vtherm_api 0.5 or newer; the plugin is tested with VT 10.4.0), so its thermostats cannot show the plugin's heat-available and emitter values. The plugin's own zone entities show them meanwhile. Update Versatile Thermostat to show them on the thermostats too.

vt_reload_needed.title: Some VT thermostats need a reload to show the plugin's values
vt_reload_needed.description: These thermostats were already running when the plugin registered with Versatile Thermostat, and pick it up only when VT reloads: {zones}. Reload Versatile Thermostat to show the plugin's heat-available and emitter values on them; the plugin's own zone entities show them meanwhile. Nothing else depends on it.

vt_central_entry_not_running.title: Versatile Thermostat's central configuration is not running
vt_central_entry_not_running.description: Its setup failed, and its settings say VT's central boiler is on. Control waits, so that two controllers never drive the boiler: fix VT's central configuration, or untick its central boiler and restart Home Assistant.

entity_removed.title: An entity the plugin uses is gone
entity_removed.description: {field}: {entity} is no longer in Home Assistant. Pick another one in the options; until then the plugin works without it.

hand_back_taken_by_other.title: After the hand-back another controller holds the boiler
hand_back_taken_by_other.description: The plugin handed the boiler back, and another controller — an automation, a device's own program or another integration — now holds what the plugin had set: {target}. The plugin counts the hand-back as done and does not write there again. With a thermostat or the boiler's own control, heating goes on under it; where the hand-back stops heating, the boiler heats only under that other controller. If you do not expect another controller, find it.

monitor_failed.title: Control handed the boiler back: the plugin's monitor keeps failing
monitor_failed.description: The plugin's monitor has failed for 5 minutes — an error in the plugin; the log has the details — so control handed the boiler back. It resumes by itself once the monitor works again. Meanwhile a thermostat or the boiler's own control heats where your installation has one; where a hand-back stops heating, the boiler does not heat until control resumes.

monitor_recovered.title: The plugin's monitor failed for a while; control has resumed
monitor_recovered.description: The plugin's monitor failed from {since} to {until}, so control handed the boiler back meanwhile. The monitor works again and control has resumed by itself. The log has the error; if this happens again, report it.

control_stopped_heating.title: Control stopped and the boiler does not heat
control_stopped_heating.description: Control handed the boiler back because something now blocks it (the control switch lists what). With this installation a hand-back stops heating: the boiler heats again when control resumes once the blocker is gone, or when you return it to its own control. Frost protection now rests on the boiler's own, if it has one.

control_latched.title: Control stepped aside: another controller writes to the boiler
control_latched.description: Another controller changed what the plugin writes to the boiler again after the plugin had written its value back once — it saw {value} on {target}, which the plugin had not written — so the plugin stepped aside and does not fight it. It handed the boiler back safely: first the lowest water temperature, then heating on where a thermostat or the boiler's own control takes over, then the release — this wrote over the other controller's value once, briefly. With a thermostat or the boiler's own control, it keeps heating; without one, the boiler heats only under the other controller. To give control back to the plugin, stop the other controller, then switch control off and on. If "Return by itself after another controller" is on, control also comes back on its own after an hour in which nothing else wrote to the boiler (not for relays).

control_latched_heating_off_ignored.title: Control stopped: the boiler does not take "heating off"
control_latched_heating_off_ignored.description: From the start of the session the boiler did not take the plugin's "heating off": the plugin could not switch heating off, so it handed the boiler back safely — first the lowest water temperature, then heating on where a thermostat or the boiler's own control takes over, then the release. Where a thermostat or the boiler's own control takes over, it heats now; where a hand-back stops heating, the boiler does not heat until control resumes. Check the heating switch picked in the options and the boiler's settings, then switch control off and on. The monitor keeps running.

control_latched_heating_on_ignored.title: Control stopped: the boiler does not take "heating on"
control_latched_heating_on_ignored.description: From the start of the session the boiler did not take the plugin's "heating on" — or the entity picked to confirm it never showed it — so the plugin could not make the boiler heat, and it handed the boiler back safely: first the lowest water temperature, then heating on where a thermostat or the boiler's own control takes over, then the release. Until control resumes the plugin does not heat the house, frost protection included: where a thermostat or the boiler's own control takes over, it heats only if the boiler takes its demand; where a hand-back stops heating, the boiler does not heat. Check the heating switch and the entity that confirms it picked in the options (a status showing whether the boiler heats right now does not confirm the switch) and the boiler's settings, then switch control off and on. The monitor keeps running.

control_latched_write_ignored.title: Control handed back: the boiler ignores a value the plugin writes
control_latched_write_ignored.description: The boiler did not take a value the plugin wrote — the alarm "Boiler ignores a value" names which — and you set that alarm to hand back. Control handed the boiler back safely: first the lowest water temperature, then heating on, then the release; the thermostat or the boiler's own control heats now. Check the entity picked in the options and the boiler's settings (a value outside its range, a setting that locks it), then switch control off and on to take the boiler back.

control_latched_other.title: Control stays handed back after an earlier alarm
control_latched_other.description: An earlier version of the plugin handed the boiler back for an alarm that now only informs ({alarm}), and control stays handed back until you switch it off and on. Where a thermostat or the boiler's own control takes over, it heats now; where a hand-back stops heating, the boiler does not heat until control resumes. Check the alarm, then switch control off and on to take the boiler back.

hand_back_boiler_link_lost.title: Control handed the boiler back: its data is lost
hand_back_boiler_link_lost.description: The boiler's flame or flow reading was not fresh for 5 minutes within 10, so control stopped writing and handed the boiler back — nothing is written without fresh data. Where a thermostat or the boiler's own control takes over, it heats now; where a hand-back stops heating, the boiler does not heat until control resumes. Control resumes by itself once the data has been fresh for a minute. Check the gateway or device, its connection and the entities picked as flame and flow.

hand_back_control_error.title: Control stopped after an internal error
hand_back_control_error.description: An error in the plugin stopped control, and it handed the boiler back — the log has the details. Where a thermostat or the boiler's own control takes over, it heats now; where a hand-back stops heating, the boiler does not heat until control resumes. Control stays stopped until you switch it off and on; if the error comes back, report it with the log.

no_zone_known_off.title: Versatile Thermostat gives no answer: the boiler is not heating
no_zone_known_off.description: None of the zones answers ({zones}), so nothing can ask for heat. The plugin keeps the boiler's heating off and resumes as soon as a zone answers. Check that Versatile Thermostat is loaded, its thermostats are enabled and their entity IDs are the ones in the plugin's options.

no_zone_known_handed_back.title: Versatile Thermostat gives no answer: the boiler is back on its thermostat or its own room controller
no_zone_known_handed_back.description: None of the zones answers ({zones}), so nothing can ask for heat. The plugin handed the boiler back to the thermostat on the gateway, or to the boiler's own room controller, and takes it again as soon as a zone answers. Check that Versatile Thermostat is loaded, its thermostats are enabled and their entity IDs are the ones in the plugin's options.

no_zone_known_monitor.title: Versatile Thermostat gives no answer
no_zone_known_monitor.description: None of the zones answers ({zones}); the monitor cannot judge them. Check that Versatile Thermostat is loaded, its thermostats are enabled and their entity IDs are the ones in the plugin's options.

no_criterion_judged_off.title: No demand criterion can be judged: the boiler is not heating
no_criterion_judged_off.description: The zones answer, but none of the demand criteria set in the plugin's options gets data from the zones that may heat, so no room's call for heat can be seen ({criteria}: "power" needs a device power set in Versatile Thermostat, "opening" a valve opening or duty cycle). The plugin keeps the boiler's heating off and resumes as soon as a criterion has data again. Set the device power in VT, or set the zone count to 1 or more in the plugin's control options.

no_criterion_judged_handed_back.title: No demand criterion can be judged: the boiler is back on its thermostat or its own room controller
no_criterion_judged_handed_back.description: The zones answer, but none of the demand criteria set in the plugin's options gets data from the zones that may heat, so no room's call for heat can be seen ({criteria}: "power" needs a device power set in Versatile Thermostat, "opening" a valve opening or duty cycle). The plugin handed the boiler back to the thermostat on the gateway, or to the boiler's own room controller, and takes it again as soon as a criterion has data again. Set the device power in VT, or set the zone count to 1 or more in the plugin's control options.

no_criterion_judged_monitor.title: No demand criterion can be judged
no_criterion_judged_monitor.description: The zones answer, but none of the demand criteria set in the plugin's options gets data from the zones that may heat, so no room's call for heat can be seen ({criteria}: "power" needs a device power set in Versatile Thermostat, "opening" a valve opening or duty cycle); switched on, control could not heat for any room. Set the device power in VT, or set the zone count to 1 or more in the plugin's control options.

frost_zone_closed.title: A room below the frost limit cannot get heat
frost_zone_closed.description: {zones}: Versatile Thermostat keeps the valve closed (the thermostat is off, or its target is below the frost limit), so the plugin cannot heat it and does not start the boiler for it. Use VT's frost preset instead of off; VT's central frost mode needs a frost temperature set in every thermostat.

thermostat_kind_missing.title: Say what is wired to the gateway's thermostat terminals
thermostat_kind_missing.description: Control of the boiler waits for the answer to a new question in the control options: what is wired to the gateway's thermostat terminals. Without a thermostat (stand-alone) the boiler does not heat meanwhile.

wall_thermostat_fallback.title: The wall thermostat would keep the house cool after a hand-back
wall_thermostat_fallback.description: The wall thermostat on the gateway is set to {value} °C. After a hand-back, or while Home Assistant is down, it heats the house by this setting and its own program. Set it to what the house should get.

wall_thermostat_fallback_unknown.title: The wall thermostat reports no setpoint
wall_thermostat_fallback_unknown.description: The wall thermostat on the gateway reports no setpoint. After a hand-back, or while Home Assistant is down, it heats the house by its own setting and program. Check that they are what the house should get, and that the wall thermostat's setpoint picked among the signals reports.

lowest_water_suggestion.title: The boiler keeps stopping at the lowest water temperature
lowest_water_suggestion.description: In the last {days} days, {short} of {burns} heating burns at about {reference} °C were shorter than {limit} min and ended because the water was warm enough, while rooms still asked for heat. Consider raising the lowest water temperature to about {value} °C in the control options. Longer burns are likely; fewer starts are not guaranteed. Nothing changes until you do.

lowest_water_suggestion_boiler.title: The boiler keeps stopping at its lowest water temperature
lowest_water_suggestion_boiler.description: In the last {days} days, {short} of {burns} heating burns at about {reference} °C were shorter than {limit} min and ended because the water was warm enough, while rooms still asked for heat. Consider raising the minimum flow temperature, or the foot point of the heating curve, of the device that sets your water temperature to about {value} °C — not the curve's parallel shift, which raises the water in frost too. Longer burns are likely; fewer starts are not guaranteed. The plugin changes nothing there.

read_back_waiting.title: Control waits for the gateway's confirmation
read_back_waiting.description: Control is switched on, but the gateway's setpoint read-back — the entity picked as the setpoint read-back in the control options — has had no value for 5 minutes, so the plugin does not take the boiler: without it, the plugin could never see that a hand-back got through. Where a thermostat or the boiler's own control takes over, it heats meanwhile; where a hand-back stops heating, the boiler does not heat until control takes it. Check that the gateway is connected and that the entity picked reports a value — the gateway's "Control setpoint 1" on its boiler device. This notice goes once the entity reports a value, or when you switch control off.

write_ignored_no_heat.title: The boiler does not accept the command: the house is not heated
write_ignored_no_heat.description: From the start of the session the boiler has not taken the water temperature the plugin writes; the alarm "Control: the boiler does not accept a command" names it. So the plugin cannot heat the house, frost protection included, and with this installation nothing else does: here a hand-back stops heating (a gateway without a thermostat gives the boiler no heat demand without the plugin's setpoint). The plugin keeps control and does not hand the boiler back; it tries the command again at the next session — when you switch control off and on, or after a restart — not when control takes the boiler again after a pause. Check the boiler's settings — a value outside its range, a setting that locks it — and the entities picked in the options, then switch control off and on.

setpoint_not_shown.title: The boiler does not show the plugin's water temperature
setpoint_not_shown.description: For 5 minutes the boiler's setpoint read-back has shown another water temperature than the one the plugin set. The plugin keeps control and does not hand the boiler back for this: the boiler may keep its own value — a limit set on it, a setting that locks it — or the entity picked as the setpoint read-back may not report the setpoint the boiler received, or report it late. Check the boiler's maximum water temperature and its control settings, and the setpoint read-back picked in the control options. Where a hand-back stops heating, the house may not get the heat it needs meanwhile. This notice goes once the read-back shows the plugin's value, or when you switch control off.

no_sign_boiler_heats.title: No sign the boiler heats
no_sign_boiler_heats.description: For {minutes} minutes control has had heating on while a room asks for heat, and the boiler has shown no sign of heating: its flame stayed off — or, without a flame signal, its flow temperature did not rise — while the water stayed below the plugin's setpoint. The boiler may be locked out after a fault, set to summer mode or with heating switched off on its own panel or in the maker's app, or without gas. Check the boiler's display for a fault or lockout code and reset it as its manual says; check that heating is switched on on the boiler's panel and in the maker's app, and that the gas supply is open. If the boiler's fault signals are available, mapping them in the options lets control see a fault at once. Control goes on and does not hand the boiler back for this. This notice goes once the flame shows on or the flow temperature rises, or when you switch control off.

relay_unreachable_off.title: The relay cannot be reached
relay_unreachable_off.description: {relay} has been out of reach for 5 minutes. The plugin cannot switch the boiler and does not hand it back, as nothing could reach the relay; it sends its command again as soon as the relay returns. Until then the relay stays as it was, or does what its own settings say: after a power cut it starts off, as you declared, so the boiler waits off.

relay_unreachable_on.title: The relay cannot be reached
relay_unreachable_on.description: {relay} has been out of reach for 5 minutes. The plugin cannot switch the boiler and does not hand it back, as nothing could reach the relay; it sends its command again as soon as the relay returns. Until then the relay stays as it was, or does what its own settings say: after a power cut it starts on, as you declared, so the boiler may heat without control.

relay_unreachable_last.title: The relay cannot be reached
relay_unreachable_last.description: {relay} has been out of reach for 5 minutes. The plugin cannot switch the boiler and does not hand it back, as nothing could reach the relay; it sends its command again as soon as the relay returns. Until then the relay stays as it was, or does what its own settings say: after a power cut it returns to its last state, as you declared, so the boiler may heat without control.

relay_unreachable_unknown.title: The relay cannot be reached
relay_unreachable_unknown.description: {relay} has been out of reach for 5 minutes. The plugin cannot switch the boiler and does not hand it back, as nothing could reach the relay; it sends its command again as soon as the relay returns. Until then the relay stays as it was, or does what its own settings say: what it does after a power cut is not known, so the boiler may heat without control.

relay_ignored.title: The relay does not accept the command — check it
relay_ignored.description: {relay} did not take the plugin's command after three tries this session. Nothing else controls the boiler now: check the relay and the entity picked in the options. The plugin tries again when control next takes the boiler. Control stays stopped until you switch it off and on.

relay_ignored_off.title: The relay does not accept the command — check it
relay_ignored_off.description: {relay} did not take the plugin's command after three tries this session. Nothing else controls the boiler now: check the relay and the entity picked in the options. The plugin tries again when control next takes the boiler. The boiler may keep heating: the relay does not switch off. Control stays stopped until you switch it off and on.

relay_not_taking.title: The relay has stopped taking commands: the house is not heated
relay_not_taking.description: {relay} took the plugin's commands earlier in this session, but for about 15 minutes — three checks — it has shown none of them, and it does not show "on" now. The boiler gets no heat demand, so the house is not heated, frost protection included. The plugin keeps control and sends "on" again at every check; this notice goes once the relay shows "on". Check the relay and its connection — a link that delivers its reports but not the commands, or a stuck contact — and the entity picked in the options.

relay_not_taking_off.title: The relay has stopped taking commands: the boiler may keep heating
relay_not_taking_off.description: {relay} took the plugin's commands earlier in this session, but for about 15 minutes — three checks — it has shown none of them, and it does not show "off" now. The boiler may keep heating, as the relay does not switch off. Control stopped; the relay was set once to its state after hand-back, which cannot be relied on either. Check the relay and its connection — a link that delivers its reports but not the commands, or a stuck contact — and the entity picked in the options, then switch control off and on. The monitor keeps running.

relay_rests_off.title: The boiler does not heat while control is off
relay_rests_off.description: Control of the boiler is off and the relay rests off, while {zones} ask for heat or are near freezing. The boiler now heats only through a thermostat wired in parallel, if you have one. Switch control on again, or change the relay's state after hand-back in the options.

relay_timer_seen.title: The relay keeps switching off a fixed time after "on"
relay_timer_seen.description: {relay} keeps switching off a fixed time after "on" — seen about {minutes} min, that time or a whole multiple of it — while its timer is set to "I don't know" in the options. This looks like the relay's own switch-off timer, but an automation that switches it off that long after "on" — a "maximum run time", say — looks the same. The plugin switches the relay on again at once each time, so heating goes on; it no longer counts these switch-offs as restarts the relay did not report, and it repeats "on" at least every half of that time, as for a declared timer, so a timer that a repeated "on" restarts no longer runs out. If it is the relay's timer, read its length in the relay's own settings and declare it in the options, or remove the timer; if it is an automation, change or remove it. Until then a switch-off at another time still counts, and a fourth within a day makes the plugin step aside.

control_latched_relay_off.title: Control stepped aside: something else switches the relay
control_latched_relay_off.description: Something else keeps switching {relay} — an automation, its own button, a person, or restarts the relay does not report. The plugin set it back; it kept changing, so the plugin stepped aside: it switched the relay off once, its state after hand-back, and now leaves it alone. The boiler heats only through a thermostat wired in parallel, if there is one. If the relay restarts without reporting it, or has its own switch-off timer, declare its state after a power cut and its timer in the options; if it restarts several times a day, check its power supply and connection. Switch control off and on to take the relay back.

control_latched_relay_on.title: Control stepped aside: something else switches the relay
control_latched_relay_on.description: Something else keeps switching {relay} — an automation, its own button, a person, or restarts the relay does not report. The plugin set it back; it kept changing, so the plugin stepped aside: it switched the relay on once, its state after hand-back, and now leaves it alone; the boiler heats by its own setting, without room control. If the relay restarts without reporting it, or has its own switch-off timer, declare its state after a power cut and its timer in the options; if it restarts several times a day, check its power supply and connection. Switch control off and on to take the relay back.

control_latched_relay_short_timer_off.title: Control stepped aside: the relay switches itself off every few minutes
control_latched_relay_short_timer_off.description: {relay} switched itself off about every {minutes} min after "on" — a switch-off timer of its own (an auto-off or "inching" mode), or an automation. A timer that short is never taken for the relay's own, as each switch-off starts the boiler again: the plugin switched the relay on again each time and counted it, and at the fourth within a day it stepped aside: it switched the relay off once, its state after hand-back, and now leaves it alone. The boiler heats only through a thermostat wired in parallel, if there is one. Set the relay's timer to at least 30 min, or switch the timer off, and declare it in the options — or change the automation. Then switch control off and on to take the relay back.

control_latched_relay_short_timer_on.title: Control stepped aside: the relay switches itself off every few minutes
control_latched_relay_short_timer_on.description: {relay} switched itself off about every {minutes} min after "on" — a switch-off timer of its own (an auto-off or "inching" mode), or an automation. A timer that short is never taken for the relay's own, as each switch-off starts the boiler again: the plugin switched the relay on again each time and counted it, and at the fourth within a day it stepped aside: it switched the relay on once, its state after hand-back, and now leaves it alone — but the relay's timer switches it off again within minutes, so the boiler may not heat at all. Set the relay's timer to at least 30 min, or switch the timer off, and declare it in the options — or change the automation. Then switch control off and on to take the relay back.

control_latched_relay_heating_off_ignore.title: Control stopped: the relay does not take "off"
control_latched_relay_heating_off_ignore.description: From the start of the session {relay} did not take the plugin's "off": the boiler may keep heating, as the relay does not switch off. Control stopped; the relay was set once to its state after hand-back, which cannot be relied on either. Check the relay and the entity picked in the options, then switch control off and on. The monitor keeps running.

control_latched_relay_heating_on_ignored.title: Control stopped: the relay does not take "on"
control_latched_relay_heating_on_ignored.description: From the start of the session {relay} did not take the plugin's "on": the boiler gets no heat demand from the plugin, so the house is not heated, frost protection included. Control stopped; the relay was set once to its state after hand-back, which cannot be relied on either. Check the relay and the entity picked in the options, then switch control off and on. The monitor keeps running.

control_latched_relay_off_not_taken.title: Control stopped: the relay stopped taking "off"
control_latched_relay_off_not_taken.description: {relay} took the plugin's commands earlier in this session, then did not show "off" for about 15 minutes: the boiler may keep heating, as the relay does not switch off. Control stopped; the relay was set once to its state after hand-back, which cannot be relied on either. Check the relay, its connection and the entity picked in the options, then switch control off and on. The monitor keeps running.

add_water.title: Heating water pressure is low — add water
add_water.description: The pressure is {value} bar, below the {threshold} bar you set from the boiler's manual. Add water with the filling tap as the manual describes, watching the boiler's gauge, then close the tap. If it keeps falling, look for a leak. Heating carries on; the boiler stops by itself if the pressure falls too far.

pressure_high.title: Heating water pressure is high
pressure_high.description: The pressure is {value} bar, above your alarm limit of {limit} bar. Your limit must be below the safety valve's rating, printed on the valve. Check that the filling tap is closed. To lower the pressure, switch the heating off and let the system cool, then let a little water out at a radiator's bleed valve until the gauge shows the cold pressure from the manual. If the pressure jumps each time the heating runs, have the expansion vessel checked; on a combi boiler, if it creeps up on its own, have the heat exchanger checked. Heating carries on.

flue_gas_high.title: Flue gas too hot
flue_gas_high.description: The flue gas is {value} °C, above your alarm limit of {limit} °C. Book a boiler service: heat exchanger, flue and condensate pipe, water circulation. The boiler's own flue protection may turn it down or lock it out. Heating carries on.

pressure_falling.title: Heating water pressure keeps falling
pressure_falling.description: Your pressure keeps falling — there is a risk of a leak. Over the last days it fell by {change} bar, with the water temperature taken into account. Look for drips at radiators, valves and the boiler, and at the safety valve's outlet; if you find none, have the system checked.

boiler_fault.title: The boiler reports a fault that stops it
boiler_fault.description: The boiler reports a fault that stops it ({entity}). The plugin keeps heating off while it does and switches it on again when the boiler clears it. Read the fault on the boiler and follow its manual.

reactions_removed.title: Alarm reactions no longer offered
reactions_removed.description: These alarm reactions are no longer offered and now only inform: {alarms}. The plugin stops heating only while the boiler itself reports a fault that stops it; the other alarms tell you what to do.

installation_empty_circuit.title: A heating circuit has no rooms
installation_empty_circuit.description: No Versatile Thermostat zone is assigned to these circuits: {circuits}. The plugin cannot tell when they need heat, and shows no critical room for them. Add their rooms in the integration's options, or remove the circuits.

installation_underfloor_without_max_flow.title: Underfloor heating without a water limit
installation_underfloor_without_max_flow.description: These circuits feed underfloor heating straight from the boiler, without a mixing valve, and have no maximum flow temperature: {circuits}. Water that is too hot can damage a floor. Enter each circuit's maximum flow temperature — the floor's limit from its installer or manual — in the integration's options; until then control stays blocked.

learning_not_resumed.title: The plugin could not switch learning back on in some zones
learning_not_resumed.description: Control paused SmartPI's learning in these zones and has not been able to switch it back on for a day, so it no longer tries: {zones}. SmartPI keeps learning off until it is switched on — in SmartPI's own settings, or with its service "set_smartpi_learning". If you switched it off yourself, nothing needs doing. This notice goes once learning is on again.
